newsitem.title: USA: Asia int. air cargo capacity growth exceeds traffi.
newsitem.headline: Asia int. air cargo capacity growth exceeds traffi.

text.p: Capacity grow faster than traffic in Asian international air cargo market last year except between the U.S.and Southeast Asia, the MergeGlobal, Inc air cargo consultancy said.

Strong Asian demand for U.S. goods resulted a 19.9 percent increase in air export traffic to Southeast Asia, versus 4.1 percent capacity growth, the consultancy's 1997 World Air Freight Analysis said.
The result was a 62 percent aggregate industry load factor for U.S.-to-Southeast Asia scheduled services, up from 54 percent in 1995.
Capacity from Southeast Asia-to-U.S. rose 5.5 percent, while traffic increased by 9.9 percent. Load factor was 71.7 percent, up from 68.8 percent.

Between North Asia and the U.S. - a market almost three times the size of U.S.-Southeast Asia - capacity was up 19.2 percent, with traffic up nine percent westbound and 4.9 percent eastbound. Load factor was 80.5 percent eastbound (-11.5 percentage points) and 76.4 percent westbound (-6.6 pts), MergeGlobal added.

Between Europe and North Asia, scheduled carriers provided 24.5 percent more capacity, while traffic grew 3.8 percent ex-Asia and 1.7 percent ex-Europe. Load factor was 63.5 percent (-14.3 pts) ex-Asia and 68.3 ex-Europe (-13.9 pts).

Between Southeast Asia and Europe, capacity rose about 8.5 percent last year, while traffic was up 2.6 percent ex-Europe and 2.7 percent ex-Asia. Load factor was 70 percent ex-Asia (-4.2 pts) and 69.3 percent ex-Europe (-3.7 percent). -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
